title: Coordinated Disentanglement with Iterative Mode Discovery Under Hidden Correlations
claim: Subtle sub-modes within a class correlate with a nuisance attribute, creating hidden correlations that mislead models beyond visible attribute correlations.
layout: Left grid of user-by-mode scatter panels; right two stacked dashed bar-chart insets
description: The left side is a 2×3 grid of gray scatter-plot tiles. Rows are users A and B, shown with avatar icons on a vertical axis labeled a2 (User ID). The top columns are activities, walking and running, under a bracket labeled a1. The bottom row labels three modes, stroll, brisk walk and run, on an axis m1, under a bracket labeled Walking mode. Each tile shows the same pale blue and red point clusters, with a different subset highlighted in saturated color. This shows how each user's samples are distributed across modes. On the right, two dashed boxes hold small bar charts. Box (a), Attribute correlations, shows each user's walking versus running frequencies. Box (b), Hidden correlations under activity walking, shows each user's stroll versus brisk walk frequencies. Dashed arrows connect the left axes to the boxes. Blue and red separate the activities, and light and dark blue separate the modes.
caption: Human activity example. The distributions of (a) “walking” / “running” and (b) “stroll” / “brisk walk” differ between users, exhibiting attribute and hidden correlations, respectively. Since the "brisk walk" mode resembles "running", a model trained under such hidden correlations may over-encode user ID to better distinguish them, i.e., associating user B with "running" on these samples, as user B hardly performs "brisk walk". Under correlation shift, e.g., when user B frequently performs "brisk walk" at test time, this may lead to misclassification.
abstract: Disentangled representation learning is a powerful paradigm for robust attribute prediction. While recent methods address attribute correlations, hidden correlations remain underexplored, where data under the value of a certain attribute exhibit underlying modes correlated with other attributes. To preserve mode information and achieve disentanglement, we jointly discover modes and enforce mode-based conditional independence. Yet, the interdependency between these two modules may lead to error amplification under naive iterations. We propose Coordinated Disentanglement with Iterative mode Discovery (CoDID), an end-to-end framework featuring a dynamic architecture that adapts to evolving number of modes, and a coordination mechanism that mitigates error amplification via meta-optimization. Empirical results demonstrate the state-of-the-art performance on diverse tasks.
